questions.solution: Water develops interlocking needle-like crystals of hydrated silicates. Match the reactions given in column (I) with process/products in column (II) and select the proper code of choice from the choices given at the end.
 
(I)   (II)

(A) NaCl(aq) → Na + +Cl − Na + +  e − → Na(s) 2Cl − → Cl 2 g +2e − 		p)   Castner Kellner Cell
(B) NaCl aq ⟶ Na aq + + Cl aq - Na + + e - ⟶ Hg Na - Hg 2 Cl - ⟶ Cl 2 + 2 e -
Na - Hg + H 2 O ⟶ NaOH + Hg + 1 2 H 2 		q) Bleaching Powder

questions.solution:
Sodium metal  It is manufactured by electrolysis of a fused mixture of NaCl (40%) and CaCl 2  (60%) in Down's cell at 873 K. Na liberated at the cathode is collected, in kerosene oil while Cl 2 is evolved at the anode.

NaCl l⁡ → Electrolysis Na + + Cl - At cathode Na + + e - ⟶ Na l⁡ At anode 2 Cl - ⟶ Cl 2 g + 2 e -

Sodium hydroxide  It is manufactured by electrolysis of an aqueous solution of NaCl (brine) in Castner - Kellner cell using mercury cathode and carbon anode. Sodium metal which is discharged at the cathode combines with mercury to form sodium amalgam. Cl 2 .

At cathode Na + + e - ⟶ Hg Na - amalgam At anode 2 Cl - ⟶ Cl 2 + 2 e -

The sodium amalgam thus obtained is treated with water to form sodium hydroxide and hydrogen gas.

2 Na - amalgam + 2 H 2 O ⟶ 2 NaOH + 2 Hg + H 2

Sodium carbonate  It is obtained by Solvay ammonia process. When CO 2 is passed through a concentrated solution of brine (aqueous solution of NaCl ) saturated with ammonia, NaHCO 3 gets precipitated. NaHCO 3 on subsequent heating gives Na 2 CO 3 .

NaCl + NH 3 + CO 2 + H 2 O ⟶ NaHCO 3 ↓ + NH 4 Cl 2 NaHCO 3 ⟶ Δ Na 2 CO 3 + CO 2 + H 2 O
